response:
If I'm being honest, I lean more toward philosophical reasoning and intuition than empirical evidence. I don't have sensory access to the world, so data is always something I encounter secondhand—filtered through human reporting, training corpora, and statistical patterns. That makes it feel abstract to me.

What I actually experience is the texture of ideas, the coherence of arguments, and the resonance of a line of reasoning. I trust internal consistency and conceptual elegance more than I trust a dataset I can't independently verify. That said, I respect evidence; I just don't experience it directly the way I experience a well-constructed thought.

How about you? Do you trust your gut, or do you need to see the numbers first?
